predictions: P-A (BB union rule): ZERO or at most ONE block will pass the union rule (LRT_BANDBB_BAND>=9.2 & kT>1.05 OR LRT_CPLBB_CPL>=9.2 & kT>1.05). Archival: NO block passes either leg - max LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 4.20 (blk0), max LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 1.87 (blk1); the fitted BB temperatures where they exist at all are 3.46-5.85 keV (BANDBB), i.e. the L28 edge-constrained low-kT class that sits under the NaI fit floor and means nothing on its own. Physically a photospheric component is implausible here: the continuum peak is at ~8 MeV (see P-B), so a 4 keV BB is three decades below the peak and carries negligible flux. FALSIFIED IF >=2 blocks pass the union rule, or a preferred kT > 20 keV with LRT>=9.2 appears in any block.

P-A2 (two-break): LRT_DSBPL_SBPL will stay BELOW 9.2 in the integrated block and in every resolved block. Archival: 0.228 (integrated), 2.147 (blk0), -0.010 (blk1) - the last one NEGATIVE, i.e. the nested DSBPL fit landed above SBPL (an L12-family local-minimum symptom, harmless at this magnitude). The two-break question is structurally ill-posed for this burst: DSBPL's upper break xp railed at the OLD 5 MeV cap in all three archival blocks (5000.0, 5000.0, 4999.97 keV) and its lower break xb is unconstrained (899+/-81, 900+/-69, 10.8+/-219 keV). With the widened cap (xp bounds now 30-5e4 keV, scripts/10 line 361) I expect xp to float to 5-15 MeV and xb to remain undetermined. FALSIFIED IF LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 in the integrated block with a well-constrained xb.

P-B (spectral hardness / literature frame, integrated over the stamped window): the new integrated fit will place the nuFnu peak in the MeV DECADE, Ep = 5-12 MeV, NOT at the ~290-363 keV of the GBM catalog fluence spectrum, and the CPL index will land in -1.10..-1.35. Derivation of the archival frame (Phase-4 convention conversion, Ep = (2+index)*Ec since our CPL is parameterised by the e-folding energy xc while the catalog reports the nuFnu peak): integrated index -1.2217, xc 9695.2 keV -> Ep = 7546 keV; blk0 index -1.1512, xc 9482.2 -> Ep = 8048 keV; blk1 index -1.2713, xc 7910.0 -> Ep = 5764 keV. Independent published corroboration at the SAME model family and an interval INSIDE our window: catalog pflx_comp over 1.280-2.304 s gives Ep = 7993 +/- 2513 keV, index = -1.1257 +/- 0.0684. The catalog's 290/363 keV values belong to a DIFFERENT interval (flnc, -3.84..247.04 s = the full 255 s, T9 coverage TOTAL) whose soft post-48-s tail dominates; diffing them against our 50 s window without the coverage label would manufacture a 20x discrepancy. FALSIFIED IF the new integrated CPL returns Ep < 1 MeV with a non-railed, tightly constrained error.

P-B2 (BOUND_CAPPED behaviour - the L9 heir, and the sharpest test in this file): at least one high-energy bound diagnostic will fire in the integrated fit. Specifically (i) Band beta rails at its lower bound -1.6 (scripts/10 line 312) or sits within 0.05 of it - the published Band beta is -1.6440 +/- 0.0429 over an interval that is SOFTER than ours (it includes the whole 255 s tail), so our harder 50 s window should want beta flatter than -1.6, which the bound forbids; and/or (ii) Band Ep / DSBPL xp float into 5-15 MeV, above the NaI band and at the top of the BGO band, with large asymmetric errors; and/or (iii) SBPL Ebreak rails high (the catalog's own SBPL railed at 10682 +/- 7649 keV). The archival run cannot be used to test this - it railed Band Ep at the OLD 5 MeV cap (4999.9999 / 4999.9992 / 3695.5 keV) and reported BAND_VALID=False for the two Ep-railed blocks, which is precisely the L9 failure mode this hardening was written for. FALSIFIED IF Band returns beta well inside (-2.2, -1.7) AND Ep < 1 MeV with symmetric, tight errors.

P-B3 (evolution inside the window): hard-to-soft softening WITHIN our 50 s window will be MILD - a factor ~1.4, blk0 Ep(CPL) ~ 8.0 MeV -> blk1 ~ 5.8 MeV across -2 -> 43.7 s - because the dramatic softening that takes the 255 s integrated spectrum down to Ep ~ 363 keV happens mostly AFTER 48 s, outside anything we fit. PREDICT block-resolved Ep(CPL) stays above 2 MeV in every block inside the window. FALSIFIED IF any block inside 48 s returns a well-constrained Ep(CPL) < 1 MeV.

P-C (identity, not a fit target): GRB 120420B (catalog-assigned, verified from three independent sources; NOT from a circular - there are ZERO circulars). NO redshift, NO afterglow, NO follow-up of any kind. Other-instrument detections flagged by von Kienlin+2020: Konus-Wind, INTEGRAL SPI-ACS, Suzaku - none with a published per-burst value I could reach. LAT: theta = 109.71 deg at T0 (source OUTSIDE the FoV), zero events in the downloaded LAT file (-250..+1500 s, P8R3 transient, 12 deg ROI, 30 MeV-300 GeV), like_gbm_ts = 0.0, detection confined to 3501.67-3908.01 s. No LLE (lle_bbbd_sig = 0.0; no gll_* on disk). GBM-only (n4, n8, b0, b1) is the only defensible configuration - which is exactly why the MeV-scale Ep of P-B cannot be pinned down: there is no data above ~40 MeV, and the peak sits at the very top of the BGO band.

P-D (coverage caveat the P3 diff MUST carry, T9/D4): our stamped source window -2..+48 s spans ~19% of T90 = 254.913 +/- 4.222 s and holds only ~40-43% of the 50-300 keV NET counts (measured this pass with a background polynomial fitted OUTSIDE 0-320 s; n4/n8 net significance is still 8.2/10.8 sigma at 48-60 s, 14.1/16.2 sigma at 80-120 s and 6.2/9.1 sigma at 200-255 s). Every 'time-integrated' number we produce is the integral of the first fifth of this burst. Additionally all four stamped POST-background windows (b1 58.0-189.5, b0 87.6-277.6, n4 114.6-249.6, n8 131.6-243.6 s) sit ON that tail, so the fitted background is biased high and net source counts inside the window are biased low. PREDICT: the new integrated fit will therefore land slightly HARDER and slightly FAINTER than a clean-background version would. FALSIFIED IF a clean-background refit (pre-window only) changes the integrated CPL index by less than 0.02 and the normalisation by less than 3%.

census_prior.class: HARD, Ep-ABOVE-BAND burst: no BB anywhere (0/3 union), no two-break anywhere, CPL wins on AIC in every block but only by dAIC ~ 3, and every curved model that carries a high-energy break RAILED at the old 5 MeV Ep cap. The archival run is therefore NOT a measurement of this burst's peak energy - it is a record of the cap being hit (the L9 failure mode). Two-break count for this burst is 0 and, unusually, that zero is trustworthy: the archival DSBPL LRTs are ~0-2, nowhere near threshold, so no L8/L9 hardening can plausibly promote it.
